The suffix addresses one finding, so an orchestrator can say \"resolve missing-context-2\". {
  "entries": [
    {
      "name": "store",
      "namespace": "topic",
      "title": "The review store",
      "body": "Every `submit-review` that reads a document writes it down. A clean review is\nstored as a review; an input that fails is stored as a rejected input — in\nseparate trees, never mixed, so the store can answer \"what was concluded\nabout this commit\" without a failure ever polluting it.\n\nStoring needs no flag and produces no output: it is simply what `submit-review`\ndoes, on every run with something to keep. The result object never mentions\nit — asking where a copy landed is `loam-refinery reviews`'s job, not\n`submit-review`'s.\n\n`store.enabled: false` in the config file is the only way to turn storing\noff. There is no per-run flag.\n\nIf the store cannot be created or written — a read-only home, a full disk, an\nunreachable `store.path` — the command exits 101, not 1 or 2. That code means\nthe machine is at fault, not the review or the invocation: revising the\nreview will not fix it, and neither will re-checking flags. Stop and report\nthe machine.\n\n`loam-refinery reviews` reads the store back: which reviews were stored for a\nrepository and commit, and, with `--failed`, which runs stored none.",
      "related": [
        "exit-codes"
      ],
      "aliases": [
        "storing"
      ],
      "provider": "topics"
    }

    {
      "name": "tiers",
      "namespace": "topic",
      "title": "Check tiers and exit codes",
      "body": "Checks come in three tiers answering different questions.\n\nStructural checks ask \"is this a document?\" — schema conformance, unique ids,\nsafe paths, well-formed refs. Always run, always hard.\n\nVerification checks ask \"is this about anything real?\" — does this path exist at\nthis ref, does the file have this many lines. Always run, and cannot be\ndisabled or demoted: an anchor claim that goes unconfirmed fails the run.\n\nAdvisory checks ask \"is this a good review?\" — a thin body, a suggestion with no\nstated cost, every comment at priority 9. Always run, never fatal outright.\n--strict promotes them to errors for the exit code; there is no flag to\nsilence one.\n\nExit 0 is valid, exit 1 means revise the review, exit 2 means fix the\ninvocation. Only document-unparseable gates the rest; otherwise one run\nreports everything findable, and checks that cannot run are listed as\nskipped, not passed.",

      "name": "verification",
      "namespace": "topic",
      "title": "Anchors as checkable claims",
      "body": "An anchor says: this path, at this commit, has this line. That is a factual\nclaim, and the one an agent gets wrong most confidently: a hallucinated line\nnumber is well-formed, plausibly numbered, and wrong.\n\nSo the document carries a ref: a full 40-character commit SHA, never a branch.\nA branch names a moving target — an anchor recorded against main means whatever\nmain points at when someone looks, stale without ever changing.\n\nvalidate checks those claims against the repository it is run in, by default and\nwith no flag, by object lookup — a commit that is not checked out still\nresolves. With no repository the tier is skipped, and reported as skipped.\n\nloam-refinery confirms the anchor points somewhere; whether it points at\nthe right line is the reviewer's job. What the SHA buys is that anyone can\ncheck:\n\n  git show 4f2c1a9:internal/fetch/client.go | sed -n '88,94p'",
